newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip, yield spreads narrow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip, yield spreads narrow.

text.p: Kicked down by stronger-than-expected housing starts, Treasuries dragged U.S. mortgage-backed securities lower in a relatively quiet Tuesday session, mortgage-market sources said.
Discount coupon pass-throughs were more prone to the weakness in Treasuries, declining about 7/32 by late afternoon. However, spreads narrowed modestly as Treasuries slipped further, traders said.
The Commerce Department reported November housing starts jumped a surprising 9.2 percent to 1.514 million units annually against a 5.1 percent drop in the previous month.
On average, Wall Street experts had forecast starts rose to a 1.390 million rate for the month.
"There were some short-dated buyers in the market earlier in the day," said one Midwest trader, referring to 15-year and balloon paper. "But now the market is dead."
She said today's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting kept many traders sidelined, though most experts forecast no change in monetary policy.
Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper fell 4/32 to 100-03/32, yielding 109 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper were 4/32 lower as well, at 99-31/32 and 100-03/32, respectively.
Looking forward, mortgage-backeds are expected to fare well in 1997, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey of 40 domestic portfolio managers.

"Many see pockets of value, such as seasoned CMOs and premium coupons, and think the sector outperforms in a steady (interest) rate environment," said money market analyst Peter McTeague, who conducts the asset allocation survey.
